note.summary: This chunk covers HMRC's Compliance Handbook general provisions on record-keeping obligations across taxes (including income tax and direct taxes claims not in a return), who counts as a 'person' for these purposes, and separate chapters on excise information notices and third-party data-gathering powers under Schedule 23 FA 2011. Record-keeping alignment changes took effect from 1 April 2009 for income tax, CGT, corporation tax, direct tax claims not in a return, and VAT, with later effective dates for other taxes. It notes a penalty may be charged for failure to keep or retain records, with no change to existing penalty regimes.

The substantive content is CH900000, an alphabetical list mapping taxes/duties to the specific returns, statements, declarations or accounts that attract inaccuracy penalties, including Income Tax and Capital Gains Tax personal returns (TMA70/S8), trustee returns (TMA70/S8A) and partnership returns. TMA 1970 ss.100-103 penalty provisions do not apply to penalties under Sch 55 FA 2009 or Sch 41 FA 2008.

Wrongdoing penalty regime applies to Landfill Tax only from 1 April 2018, though page titles in that section don't reflect this.

note.summary: This chunk covers HMRC's compliance handbook standard of proof (balance of probabilities) for careless/deliberate behaviour, then overviews three penalty regimes: failure to file returns on time (Schedule 55 FA 2009, covering Income Tax, CGT, CIS, PAYE RTI and other taxes), failure to notify (Schedule 41 FA 2008), and VAT/excise/landfill wrongdoing penalties (also Schedule 41 FA 2008 and Schedule 12 FA 2018). All regimes feature reasonable excuse defences, penalty assessments with appeal/review rights, special reduction for special circumstances, and disapplication of TMA 1970 ss.100-103.

This content relates to interest rules generally (applicable to VAT and other taxes) rather than being specific to Self Assessment Income Tax, though late payment/repayment interest concepts may be relevant to SA if/when the regime applies to Income Tax.

definitions.meaning: Interest charged when a person pays late, running from the late payment interest start date (usually the date the amount is due and payable) to the late payment interest end date (usually the date paid or set off), calculated on a simple basis.
Interest paid by HMRC on overpayments and repayments, running from the repayment interest start date to the repayment interest end date (date repaid or set off), calculated on a simple basis.

For amounts paid to HMRC and then repaid, the later of the date the amount was paid and the date the amount being repaid was due and payable; applies to all taxes covered by FA2009 interest provisions.

For amounts not paid to HMRC but becoming payable via a return or claim, the later of the date the return/claim was required and the date it was actually filed/made; currently only applies to VAT from 01/01/2023 for Prescribed Accounting Periods starting on or after 01/01/2023.
Recompense for the loss of use of money over time; it is not a penalty.

obligations.must: pay the correct amount due under an enactment to HMRC by the due and payable date
obligations.who: A person owing tax or duty

note.summary: This chunk explains the FA 2009 interest rules regime, which apply to certain taxes (not yet all) and replace previous interest provisions where applicable. It sets out general rules for calculating late payment interest (simple, from a start date to end date) and repayment interest (with two start-date rules depending on whether an amount was paid to HMRC or arises from a return/claim), noting Rule 2 currently only applies to VAT from 01/01/2023. It also describes CH140110 as a navigational page explaining how to use the interest guidance, pointing to general rules and special provisions elsewhere in the manual.

caveats: Aligned time limits do not affect the rules on how long HMRC has to make an assessment (a distinct concept from how far back it can assess).
Transitional provisions apply for VAT (from 1 April 2009) and for direct taxes/other duties (from 1 April 2010), and for SDLT/SDRT/PRT/excise duty (from 1 April 2011).
Aligned time limits apply to assessments made after the relevant commencement dates regardless of the period to which the assessment relates.
This guidance covers assessments/determinations and IHT recovery proceedings, not time limits for claims, which are covered elsewhere.

There are no consequential claims permitted for VAT, IPT, aggregates levy, climate change levy, landfill tax, PRT or excise duty following a discovery assessment/enquiry closure, unlike for IT/CGT/CT/SDLT.
Restrictions exist on use of the 12-year offshore time limit, e.g. where HMRC received relevant overseas information (see CH53510, CH53550).
For IHT where no account has been delivered, if loss of tax is brought about deliberately, there remains no time limit at all.
Onus of proof for careless or deliberate behaviour rests with HMRC, relevant when extended time limits are invoked.

note.summary: This chunk explains HMRC's aligned assessment time limits across taxes (from 1 April 2010 for direct taxes), distinguishing normal time limits from extended limits for careless behaviour (6 years), deliberate behaviour (20 years), and offshore matters (12 years). It also sets out special time limits for assessing personal representatives of deceased persons for income tax/CGT (4 years from end of year of assessment of death, or 6 years back for careless/deliberate behaviour) and VAT, and confirms HMRC bears the onus of proving careless or deliberate behaviour when relying on extended time limits.
